question.text: 'Himalaya Mezzanine Debt AIF' has only 8 LPs, each of whom has committed ₹85 crore. Under the PPM framework, what exemption pathway is available to this fund?

answer.text: Exemption from the minimum prescribed PPM disclosures and annual audit, provided each investor commits at least ₹70 crore (USD 10 million) and also provides a waiver to the fund in the prescribed manner.
Automatic exemption from the PPM filing and annual audit requirements.
Exemption only from SEBI's comments on the PPM, but annual audit remains mandatory.
No exemption — the fund must comply with all PPM disclosures and audit obligations regardless of commitment size.

explanation.text: The Logic: The workbook (page 190) specifies that AIFs/schemes in which each investor commits a minimum of ₹70 crore (USD 10 million or equivalent in non-INR currency) AND the investor provides a waiver to the fund — in the prescribed manner — from the SEBI-template PPM and the annual PPM audit are exempt from those requirements. 'Automatic' without an investor waiver is incorrect; LVF is a different exemption basis altogether. The Trap: Exemption is not automatic — the waiver must be affirmatively provided by each LP in the prescribed manner. Partial exemption (only from SEBI comments) is not the framework, and full compliance regardless of size ignores the carve-out. Note: Use only the workbook elements — ₹70 crore / USD 10 million per-investor threshold and prescribed-waiver mechanic — without adding audit-holiday planning prescriptions.
